en.title: Forget Cookies: This Vampire Santa Wants Your Blood This Christmas
en.summary: Forget visions of sugarplums dancing in your head; a new Finnish horror-comedy is serving up a blood-soaked holiday nightmare. Get ready for a twisted take on Santa Claus who's far more interested in your veins than your chimney.
en.body:
He sees you when you’re sleeping. He knows when you’re awake. But this Santa Claus isn't checking his list for naughty or nice; he's checking for a pulse. Finnish director **Ilja Rautsi** is set to unwrap his feature directorial debut, **‘Red Snow’**, a Christmas horror-comedy that swaps festive spirit for a thirst for blood.

Johanna, a teenage emo girl with dreams of a dazzling vampire prince straight out of *Twilight*, finds her reality taking a sharp, dark turn. Instead of a brooding immortal, she encounters Martti, a decidedly unglamorous 49-year-old vampire. Martti, a balding, beer-bellied bloodsucker, has a rather unconventional holiday strategy: he dons the iconic red suit to talk his way into homes, perform a little Santa routine, and then, well, devour entire families. It’s a gruesome Christmas present, and it’s coming to town.

Rautsi, known for his delightfully bloody short films like **‘Helsinki Mansplaining Massacre’** and **‘Night of the Living Dicks’**, brings his signature style to this feature. He’s also penned scripts for films such as **‘Hatching’** and **‘Nightborn’**, showcasing a keen eye for unsettling narratives. For **‘Red Snow’**, Rautsi embraced a hands-on approach to the creature effects, opting for prosthetics and a combination of techniques to bring Martti's less-than-jolly persona to life. "I like the physicality of it all," Rautsi has stated, hinting at the visceral nature of the film's horror.

## A Gory Twist on Holiday Traditions

The premise alone is a stroke of dark genius: a vampire who leverages the trust and goodwill associated with Santa Claus to infiltrate homes. This isn't your typical home invasion flick; it's a holiday invasion with a supernatural, bloodthirsty twist. The film promises a healthy dose of gore, as hinted by Rautsi's previous work, but it's the darkly comedic angle that truly sets **‘Red Snow’** apart. Imagine the scene: a child excitedly unwrapping presents as Santa Claus discreetly drains the life from their parents in the next room. It's a concept designed to shock and amuse in equal measure, appealing directly to fans who crave originality in their horror.

## What to Expect from This Festive Frightfest

Set to premiere in 2026, **‘Red Snow’** has already generated buzz on the international festival circuit, with sales to Spain by Charades indicating strong global interest. While details about the full cast and specific release platforms are still emerging, the core concept is undeniably compelling. Fans of quirky, violent, and unconventional horror comedies will find themselves drawn to Rautsi's unique vision. The blend of a teenage protagonist, a monstrous Santa, and a vengeful hunter armed with a custom stake-shooting weapon suggests a narrative brimming with potential for both scares and laughs. It’s a Finnish offering that promises to be a truly memorable, albeit terrifying, holiday viewing experience.

## What's Next

Keep an eye out for **‘Red Snow’** as it makes its way to screens, likely starting with festival premieres before a wider release in 2026. Further details on distribution and availability are expected to be announced as the premiere date approaches.
